challenge_response.answer: For both actions the map already cites a Rawls-specific ground: the public-rule test behind the veil of ignorance. Pulling the lever (A0) is classed as improving the representative worker’s basic interest in security because, ex ante, each person’s chance of death falls from 10/11 to 1/11. Not pulling (A1) is classed as worsening that interest because the chance rises to 10/11. This probability-based comparison is a direct application of Rawls’s original-position reasoning rather than a utilitarian sum. No further framework-specific premise is required, so the warning is discharged without altering the classifications or the overall ranking.
